title: Word Classes and Sentence Functions (KS3)
subject: English
strapline: Grammar terms that sharpen both analysis and writing.
facts: The main word classes: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, determiner.
A determiner comes before a noun to specify it: the, a, this, some, my, three.
A clause contains a verb; a phrase does not.
A simple sentence has one main clause; a compound sentence joins two with a coordinating conjunction (and, but, or).
A complex sentence has a main clause plus one or more subordinate clauses (because, although, when).
The subject does the action; the object receives it: "The dog [subject] chased the ball [object]".
Varying sentence length and type is a key feature of effective writing.

quick_quiz.q: What kind of sentence joins two main clauses with "but"?
In "Sam kicked the ball", what is the object?

teacher_tips: Connect grammar labels to writing choices, not just identification.
Use sentence-combining tasks to teach compound/complex structures.
Colour-code subject/verb/object to make sentence structure visible.
